newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Kelley wary of hasty cybermoney regulation.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Kelley wary of hasty cybermoney regulation.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Edward Kelley said Thursday that regulators should be in no hurry to enter the growing retail sector of electronic money transactions.
"The challenge for the regulators is not to mess it up. You know there is some history of that happening," Kelley said in a speech to the Bank Holding Company Association here.
Electronic mony, or cybermoney, involves financial transactions either over the Internet or using so-called "smart" cards which store value on a small computer chip.

"It's the private sector that's got to play the critical role in identifying which services consumers and businesses want and are willing to pay for in the areas of stored value or smart cards and in the development of access capabilities," he said.
"We believe that heavyhanded, preemptive attempts to regulate these products before any social risks have been demonstrated would handicap innovation," Kelley said.

"On the other hand, if significant problems affecting the economic interests and well being of any group of citizens were to arise, there would have to be a corresponding legislative and regulatory response," he said.
